Key Research Thinking Patterns: Spectral Trace Analysis: Utilizing local and global trace formulas for Atkin-Lehner operators to derive asymptotic biases and equidistribution properties of root numbers in modular forms.

Geometric Parametrization: Constructing explicit Weierstrass models and rational parametrizations for genus 2 curves with real multiplication by applying conic bundle minimization and blow-up singularity resolution.

Arithmetic Field Classification: Classifying rationality fields of CM forms by analyzing Grössencharacter value fields, ray class group structures, and ideal capitulation to prove finiteness conjectures under the Extended Riemann Hypothesis.

Computational Verification: Leveraging high-performance computing (ICERM OSCAR) and databases (LMFDB, SageMath) to validate theoretical predictions on murmurations of Fourier coefficients and conductor bounds.
Summary Description: Kimball Martin bridges analytic number theory and arithmetic geometry, specializing in modular forms, genus 2 curves, and complex multiplication. He employs trace formulas to analyze root number distributions and characterizes 'murmurations' in Fourier coefficients. His work extends to CM forms, proving finiteness conjectures for rationality fields of bounded degree under the Extended Riemann Hypothesis. By analyzing Grössencharacter value fields and ray class groups, he explicitly classifies quadratic and cubic rationality fields for weight 2 CM forms. This research connects modular forms to abelian varieties of GL(2) type, providing constructive insights into endomorphism algebras and minimal fields of definition, significantly expanding the toolkit for studying arithmetic properties of automorphic representations and their associated geometric moduli.
